title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
gist: Open-source Windows clone ReactOS can now be installed directly onto an NTFS partition, ending its FAT32-only install requirement and a gap of nearly a decade since read-only NTFS support arrived in 2016. The driver still lacks caching, journaling, and security support, and the volunteer-driven project remains in alpha.

insights.claim: ReactOS can now be installed directly onto an NTFS partition, removing the FAT32 requirement for installs and moving the project closer to beta.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: This is a small step toward a credible open-source binary-compatible Windows alternative, which matters for legacy-app and anti-lock-in use cases.

insights.claim: NTFS support was needed for ReactOS's goal of binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, because the XP-era NTFS variant is still the standard on most Windows systems.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Filesystem parity is a prerequisite before any drop-in Windows replacement can work.

insights.claim: The ReactOS NTFS work took nearly a decade: read-only support landed in 2016, FreeLoader bootloader support in 2022, and install support only now.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Progress is very slow, so expect any real threat to Windows to be years away at best.

insights.claim: The new ReactOS NTFS driver lacks caching (which hurts performance), journaling, and security support, and may have undiscovered bugs.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: It is not production-ready, and it is a data-integrity risk for anyone who tries it.
